question.nlq: I would like to know the names of senior employees who are employed at companies whose market value is greater than the average market value of all companies.
evidence: A good profit margin is defined as a profit-to-sales ratio exceeding 10 percent.
Senior employee: an employee who has worked for the same company for at least 3 years (i.e., Year_working >= 3).

meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT p."Name"
FROM "people" p
JOIN "employment" e ON p."People_ID" = e."People_ID"
JOIN "company" c ON e."Company_ID" = c."Company_ID"
WHERE e."Year_working" >= 3
  AND c."Market_Value_in_Billion" > (SELECT AVG("Market_Value_in_Billion") FROM "company");

question.nlq: Could you tell me which companies have a high profit margin?
evidence: In this context, a 'high profit margin' is defined as a profit margin greater than 20%, where profit margin = (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) × 100.
A 'mega‑cap' company is one whose market value exceeds 200 billion dollars.

turns.sql: SELECT Name FROM company WHERE (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 > 20;

SELECT Name FROM company WHERE (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 > 20

SELECT Name,
       (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 AS profit_margin
FROM company
WHERE Sales_in_Billion <> 0
  AND (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 > 20
ORDER BY profit_margin DESC;

FROM company

ORDER BY profit_margin DESC;

question.nlq: Identify all companies classified as financially strong based on their annual performance metrics.
evidence: Financial strength is determined by profit margin threshold. A company is considered financially strong if its profit margin (calculated as Profits_in_Billion divided by Sales_in_Billion multiplied by 100) exceeds 15 percent.
Return on Assets (ROA) is calculated as Profits_in_Billion divided by Assets_in_Billion multiplied by 100, and is used to measure how efficiently a company utilizes its assets to generate profit.

turns.sql: SELECT Name FROM company WHERE (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 > 15;
SELECT Name FROM company WHERE (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 > 15;
SELECT Name FROM company WHERE (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 > 15
SELECT Company_ID, Name, Headquarters, Industry, Sales_in_Billion, Profits_in_Billion, Assets_in_Billion, Market_Value_in_Billion FROM company WHERE (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion * 100) > 15
SELECT "Name" FROM "company" WHERE "Sales_in_Billion" > 0 AND ("Profits_in_Billion" * 100.0 / "Sales_in_Billion") > 15
SELECT Name FROM company WHERE Sales_in_Billion > 0 AND (Profits_in_Billion * 100.0 / Sales_in_Billion) > 15

SELECT
    Company_ID,
    Name,
    (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 AS profit_margin,
    (Profits_in_Billion / Assets_in_Billion) * 100 AS ROA
FROM company
WHERE Sales_in_Billion <> 0
  AND ((Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100) > 15;

SELECT
    Company_ID,
    Name,
    (Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100 AS profit_margin,
    (Profits_in_Billion / Assets_in_Billion) * 100 AS ROA
FROM company
WHERE Sales_in_Billion <> 0
  AND ((Profits_in_Billion / Sales_in_Billion) * 100) > 15;
